draft.title: Inflation
card: Inflation is a general rise in prices over time. It is about prices across the economy, not one item.
In Australia, inflation is measured by the consumer price index (CPI). The CPI tracks the cost of a basket of goods and services that households buy.
When prices rise in general, each dollar buys less than before. This is a fall in what money can buy.
The inflation rate is the percentage change in the CPI over a period, often a year.
draft.remember: Inflation is a general rise in prices, so each dollar buys less.

a.q: What does inflation mean for a dollar?
opts: It buys less than before
It buys more than before
It buys the same as before
It becomes worth more to savers
a.why: When prices in general rise, the same dollar buys fewer goods and services. Buying more would happen if prices fell.
a.clue: Think about what happens when prices rise.

b.q: In one year, the price of mangoes in Darwin jumps because of a poor harvest. Most other prices stay about the same. Is this inflation?
opts: No, because prices in general have not risen
Yes, because one price has risen
Yes, because mangoes are in the CPI basket
No, because inflation only counts services
b.why: Inflation is a general rise in prices, not a rise in one item. A single price change that is not matched by others does not show inflation. Inflation counts goods as well as services.
b.clue: Inflation is about prices in general.

b.best: No, because prices in general have not risen
